answer: Trade volume is capped at exactly ten times each identity's locked stake per epoch, so a swarm splitting one bond across a hundred fakes moves no more total volume than a single honest trader. Like a tide, honest capacity rises only as stake deepens; a gale of fresh fakes cannot outrun the cap. The stake is a visible plume of real capital: fraud burns half of it and repays victims, so scaling an attack means locking more money, not inventing more names.
